Consult Summary:
- Telephone consult for acute neurologic symptoms: patient awoke ~1 hour prior with inability to move left arm, left facial tingling, difficulty drinking/swallowing, and speech difficulty.
- GP concerned for acute stroke; emergency ambulance arranged to transport patient to ED for urgent stroke assessment. Patient advised to unlock door and wait; GP remained on the line pending ambulance arrival.

Problem List:

Issue 1:
- Suspected acute stroke
- Timeline/symptoms: On waking ~1 hour before call; persistent inability to move left arm. No arm pain, no discoloration, no coldness. Left facial tingling. Difficulty drinking/swallowing. Speech feels slower/harder; patient needs to think more before speaking. Symptoms ongoing and speech worsening during call.
- Pertinent negatives: No symptoms in left leg.
- Examination context: Telephone consult; no visual exam. Patient denies noticing facial asymmetry.
- Risk factors: Type 2 diabetes; hypertension; former smoker; alcohol intake; family history of heart disease (father).
- Plan during consult: Emergency ambulance dispatched for transfer to ED. Anticipated ED stroke team assessment (“they will ring through for the stroke doctor”). Safety advice to unlock front door and wait in hallway; GP stayed on line.
